# SelfShelf

> SelfShelf (www.selfshelf.in) is a free digital bookshelf and reading tracker that runs in the web browser. Readers put their books on real-looking shelves in a virtual room they decorate, track what they read, set a yearly reading goal, and keep a journal with ratings, reviews and saved quotes for every book. It is made in India as an independent project.

Key facts:

- Price: free to use. No app download needed; works on phone, tablet and computer browsers, and can be added to a phone's home screen.
- Reading statuses: Want to read, Reading, Finished, Did not finish, plus favourites.
- Reading tracking: current page, yearly reading goal, reading streak, and a yearly "wrapped" summary.
- Journal: ratings with half stars, written reviews, tags, start and finish dates, and quotes with page numbers.
- Adding books: search by title, author or ISBN (data from Open Library and Google Books), add by hand with a photo of the cover, or import a whole Goodreads library from its CSV export (ratings, reviews, dates read and shelves come across).
- Virtual room: shelves of spines, covers, leaning and stacked books; room styles such as cottagecore, dark academia and Japandi; decor objects; multiple rooms.
- Privacy: shelves are private by default. A public shelf link (selfshelf.in/s/@username) and a shareable shelf picture are optional, and owners choose whether reviews and quotes are visible.
- Good fit for: readers looking for a visual alternative to Goodreads, The StoryGraph or LibraryThing; people who want a reading journal or a "bookshelf aesthetic".
